holidays.name: National Cheese Lovers Day
holidays.description: A day for dairy devotees to indulge in everything from sharp cheddar to stinky blue cheese. Fondue pots, grilled cheese sandwiches, and charcuterie boards are all fair game.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, food-industry-popularized observance in the United States, spread largely through social media and cheese-loving communities rather than any government proclamation.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 10 pounds of milk to make just one pound of cheese, and the average American eats over 40 pounds of cheese per year.

holidays.name: Penguin Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate our tuxedo-wearing, waddling friends of the southern hemisphere. People celebrate by learning about penguins, wearing black and white, or visiting a zoo or aquarium.
holidays.origin: Often attributed to Northern Illinois University, where it was reportedly started in 1970s as a way to brighten up the dreary middle of winter, and it has since spread worldwide.
holidays.funFact: Penguins propose to their mates by presenting them with a carefully selected pebble, and many species mate with the same partner for years.

holidays.name: Buttercrunch Day
holidays.description: A sweet salute to the crunchy, buttery toffee candy typically covered in chocolate and chopped nuts. It is a day for snapping off a piece and enjoying the satisfying crack.
holidays.origin: A confectionery-themed unofficial observance, part of the many candy-related days on the American calendar, celebrating a classic toffee confection that dates back generations.
holidays.funFact: Toffee-style candy gets its signature crunch from being cooked to the 'hard crack' stage, around 300 degrees Fahrenheit.

holidays.name: Inauguration Day (Every Four Years) and Get to Know Your Customers Day
holidays.description: Alongside the pomp of presidential swearing-in ceremonies in the U.S., a quieter business-minded observance encourages companies to actually talk to the people who buy their stuff, rather than just guess what they want.
holidays.origin: Inauguration Day was moved to January 20 by the 20th Amendment, ratified in 1933. Get to Know Your Customers Day was created as a business-community observance, held on the third Thursday of January.
holidays.funFact: When January 20 lands on a Sunday, as in 1985 and 2013, the president takes a private oath that day and a public ceremony is held on Monday.

holidays.name: National Disc Jockey Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the people who spin the records, curate the playlists, and keep dance floors packed, from radio hosts to wedding DJs and club legends.
holidays.origin: An unofficial celebration of the art of the DJ, tied to the history of radio and recorded music broadcasting that began in the early twentieth century.
holidays.funFact: The term 'disc jockey' was first used in 1935 by radio commentator Walter Winchell to describe a person who 'rides' records the way a jockey rides a horse.
